tasks.verification_boundary: J45 public protocol evidence covers negative/zero startRevision cases, negative watch ID Create/Cancel, future startRevision Create/Cancel, and the Compact-boundary lifecycle. Future-event delivery, positive historical startRevision behavior, and replay/live handoff are assigned to J46.1. The native raw-proto event probe waits for etcd's synced progress marker as a harness barrier; this does not claim Java progress-request support, which is assigned to J46.2. Native raw-proto and local-service Go traces compare the registered start/cancel matrix; a separate Go-client lifecycle run exercises multiple watch IDs, byte ranges, filters/PrevKV, and client-context cancellation cleanup against Java WatchService, including two concurrently requested watchers sharing one pinned client stream. Normal server-side request half-close semantics remain assigned to J47. MiniCluster acceptance remains outside this unit evidence

J46.1 validates inclusive positive historical replay, per-revision ordinal ordering, compaction registration races, and deterministic replay-to-live handoff at the captured (sequence, ordinal) barrier. J46.2 validates explicit and periodic progress barriers, event-before-progress ordering, filtered revisions, incomplete history, future starts, and the pinned etcd v3.5.23 raw-proto oracle. J46.3 validates bounded revision fragmentation, ordering and cancellation cleanup, plus the pinned Go client's fragment reassembly, automatic reconnection after first- and middle-fragment interruptions, and resumption at the next revision after a disconnect following a complete fragmented revision. Both recovery boundaries use the same Watch channel and verify replay-to-live handoff against Java WatchService on HBase MiniCluster with HISTORY and NATIVE layouts.

J47 validates startup readiness after event-index backfill and tailer installation, revokes readiness when the history worker fails or the tailer closes, and rejects event-history protection from another registry before storage reads. Production Lease activation requires the J51 identity, recovery and health capabilities; only trusted test wiring may select the public test profile. J47 then validates per-watch budget isolation when a transport is not ready, accepted asynchronous Watch creates across client half-close, Created-to-Canceled compact_revision delivery during historical replay, and cleanup after request-stream errors, client cancellation, deadline, late callbacks, physical producer drain and durable history-pin release. A real MiniCluster collector test opens WatchHistoryReplay against a durable event-pin registry and proves that the required EVENT row remains until replay settles, then becomes collectible after backfill and safe-watermark advancement. A pinned Go client also keeps an active Watch open after request-side half-close, then verifies that RuntimeServer shutdown terminates the RPC and that event-tailer HBase read counters remain stable after runtime, background identity provider, and request cleanup drain on both HBase MiniCluster layouts. This covers the existing shutdown lifecycle only; credential rotation/generation invalidation and cross-replica propagation remain assigned to J51. A pinned Go etcd client exercises the Milvus sessionutil registration shape against Java WatchService on both HBase MiniCluster layouts: one atomic multi-role registration binds expiring service keys, leaves the coordinator version key unleased, lists services at revision R, watches from R+1, renews at TTL/3, applies PrevKV deletes to local service lists, and preserves a role rebound to another Lease. A combined load case interleaves periodic KeepAlive between business writes while a Watch client is not reading, then replays the committed history through a bounded watcher burst. This is an isolated consumer fixture, not complete Milvus deployment acceptance. This evidence does not claim target credential rotation, production fanout capacity, or target-cluster acceptance.
